title: [Audit] 🎛️ Command Center
description: Entry point for Cloud Audit Dashboards. KPIs, volume, actor risk and the live signal feed.

config.content:
### See who did what across your Elastic Cloud projects

This overview shows how much activity there was, who was busiest, which identities carry the most risk, and the latest events as they arrive.

Start here for a routine review or when something looks wrong, then use the links above to go deeper on one person, sign-ins, Kibana objects, data access, security or location.

**How to use it:** choose a Project, Person (email), API key or Client IP in the controls to focus every panel, and set the time picker. Raw records: [All audit events](/app/discover#/view/cloud-audit-search-00-all-events), [Raw signal feed](/app/discover#/view/cloud-audit-search-10-raw-signal-feed).

- Risk is weight × events, from 10 for a workflow run to 50 for a security change, so it runs far above event counts.
- An API key carries its creator’s email, so a person’s row can include a machine’s traffic (“email · via key”).
- Click a Principal id to filter the page or open Actor 360; a Cloud API key’s id also covers the API keys it created.
- A Client IP marked *internal* is Kibana or the platform acting for someone, not where they are.
- The last time bucket is partial, and panels side by side can differ by an event or two at the edges of the range.

config.description: Every audited event in range, routine machine traffic included. Compare with Signal events to see how much the noise gate removes. The line above the number compares it with the prior period of the same length.

Events left after the noise gate removes routine traffic: health checks, the background requests behind searches and page loads, API key lookups, bulk sign-in records and these dashboards' own activity.

config.description: Security configuration changes (API keys created, changed or invalidated; roles and user profiles written) by anyone, all traffic. Kibana’s routine API-key clean-up is left out; the line above the number counts it. Any other non-zero value deserves review.

config.title: Audit volume by source · all traffic
config.description: Total audited events over time, by source service. Elasticsearch usually far outweighs Kibana, but Kibana holds most of the forensic value. The last bar is partial; a gap means no events were delivered for that bucket.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY BUCKET(@timestamp, 75, ?_tstart, ?_tend), source = service.name | EVAL source = CASE(source == "serverless-elasticsearch", "Elasticsearch", source == "serverless-kibana", "Kibana", source) | SORT source

config.content:
### How to read this suite

**Routine traffic is left out** unless a panel title says *all traffic*. That covers health checks, the background requests behind each search and page load, API key lookups, bulk sign-in records, and these dashboards' own activity.

**Each identity is named** by its email address, or the API key's name when there is no email, or a numeric user ID as a last resort.

**Cloud API keys have no name** in the audit log, so they appear by the start of their ID, such as `_4KEO… · Cloud API key`.

**Locations use the real client address,** not Elastic's own network hops. *Hover the ⓘ beside a panel title for details.*

config.description: How far back this project's audit stream goes: its first stored event and the days since. It ignores the time picker and the controls. The retention line is the data stream's setting, read when the dashboards were installed.

config.title: Actor footprint · area by √events, color by risk total
config.description: The busiest identities as tiles, grouped by kind: named API key, person, Cloud API key, platform, user without email, unattributed. Bigger means more activity, but read the printed count, not the area. Stronger color means more risk.

config.title: Signal vs noise over time · all traffic
config.description: Every bucket split into Signal, what the noise gate keeps, and Noise, the routine traffic it removes. Log scale: each gridline is ten times the one below, so read the gap between the bars as a ratio.

(event.action IN ("saved_object_get","saved_object_resolve","saved_object_find") OR kibana.session.id IS NULL))) | EVAL band = CASE(elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("cluster:monitor/main", "indices:data/read/scroll*" OR elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/*point_in_time" OR elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/open_reader_context" OR elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/esql*" OR elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:admin/esql/*" OR elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/field_caps*" OR elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "authn-volume", "signal") | EVAL side = CASE(band == "signal", "Signal", "Noise") | STATS events = SUM(n) BY ts, side | EVAL ord = CASE(side == "Signal", 0, 1) | SORT ord, ts

config.title: Event categories · all traffic
config.description: Event categories across all traffic, routine included. Log scale: read each bar’s count, not its length. An event can belong to two categories, so the bars sum to more than the total; “none recorded” means no category.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY category = event.category | EVAL category = COALESCE(category, "none recorded") | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 8 | EVAL category = CONCAT(category, " · ", CASE(LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 3, TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 6, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) <= 9, CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 6), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)), CONCAT(LEFT(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 9), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 8, 3), ",", SUBSTRING(TO_STRING(events), LENGTH(TO_STRING(events)) - 5, 3), ",", RIGHT(TO_STRING(events), 3)))) | KEEP category, events

config.title: Live signal feed · Kibana key clean-up left out
config.description: The newest 200 signal events, with routine traffic and Kibana’s own key clean-up left out. Long runs of near-identical rows from one identity are automation: pick a Person, or filter it out in Discover, to read past it.
